About Us

We're building the future of accounting. Our AI-powered agentic platform automates complex financial workflows — from reconciliation and audit prep to tax compliance and advisory — so accountants can focus on the work that actually matters. Backed by top-tier investors, we're a small, fast-moving team shipping product at a pace that would make most startups jealous.

The Role

We're looking for a Software Engineering Intern who's excited to build real features, ship real code, and see their work in the hands of real users — all in a single summer. You won't be working on a side project no one looks at. You'll be embedded in one of our product squads, contributing directly to our core platform alongside senior engineers, designers, and domain experts.

By the end of the summer, you'll have owned a meaningful project from scoping through delivery, presented your work to the company, and gained deep exposure to how AI agents, LLMs, and modern infrastructure come together to solve hard problems in finance.

What You'll Do

- Design, build, and ship features across our full stack (React/TypeScript front end, Python/FastAPI back end, PostgreSQL)

- Work with LLM orchestration frameworks to develop, test, and improve our AI accounting agents

- Collaborate with accountants and domain experts to understand real-world workflows and translate them into product

- Write clean, well-tested code and participate in code reviews with experienced engineers

- Tackle ambiguous problems — we'll give you ownership, context, and support, not a step-by-step playbook

- Present your summer project to the full team at the end of the internship

What We're Looking For

- Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field (expected graduation 2027 or later)

- Strong fundamentals in at least one programming language (Python, TypeScript/JavaScript, Go, or similar)

- Familiarity with web development concepts (APIs, databases, front-end frameworks)

- Genuine curiosity about AI/ML, large language models, or agentic systems — prior project work or coursework is a plus, not a requirement

- Comfort with ambiguity and a bias toward action — you'd rather ship an imperfect v1 than deliberate forever

- Strong communication skills and a collaborative mindset

Bonus Points

- Experience with LLM APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.) or prompt engineering

- Exposure to accounting, fintech, or enterprise SaaS

- Contributions to open-source projects

- Familiarity with cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP) or containerization (Docker, Kubernetes)

Why Join Us

- Real impact: Your code will be in production, used by accountants at real firms, before you go back to school.

- Learn fast: Daily exposure to AI agents, LLM engineering, and complex financial domain problems — the kind of experience that's hard to get anywhere else.

- Great team: Small enough that everyone knows your name, senior enough that you'll learn from every conversation.

- Career launchpad: Strong interns receive full-time return offers. Several of our current engineers started as interns.

About Zipline

Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products.

Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations.

Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe.

We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds.

About the Launch & Scale Team

The Launch & Scale team builds the operating system that brings new sites, metros, and partners online and helps the network scale reliably. We turn complex dependencies into clear launch plans, readiness mechanisms, tools, and operating rhythms. We partner across infrastructure, permitting, flight operations, maintenance, commercial, partner readiness, and field operations. Our work stays close to real launches so that field lessons become repeatable systems rather than one-off fixes. As an intern, you will report to the Director, Launch & Site Operations and work closely with Launch Managers and cross-functional teams that bring the network online.

The Role

As the Launch & Scale Intern, you will contribute to a high-impact project that improves how Zipline plans, executes, and learns from launches. You will support Launch Managers by bringing structure to dependencies, analyzing readiness and performance, and helping teams turn field lessons into repeatable tools. You may spend time close to active launches, but you will work with experienced teammates rather than serve as the accountable launch owner. You will also own a clearly scoped project—such as a dashboard, process improvement, playbook, or lightweight automation—from problem definition through pilot and handoff. Along the way, you will receive coaching from the Director, Launch & Site Operations and collaborate with operators, engineers, commercial teammates, and field teams.

What You'll Do

- Support integrated launch plans for assigned workstreams by organizing milestones, dependencies, owners, risks, and open decisions.

- Analyze launch and site-operations data to identify bottlenecks, inconsistencies, and opportunities to improve speed, quality, or repeatability.

- Prepare materials for readiness reviews and operating forums, including concise status summaries, action logs, and decision briefs.

- Work with Launch Managers and functional teams to follow up on commitments, reconcile conflicting information, and surface blockers early.

- Build or improve practical tools such as dashboards, playbooks, templates, checklists, or lightweight automations.

- Participate in selected onsite launch activities, capture field observations, and translate lessons into process improvements.

- Own a scoped internship project from problem definition through pilot, measurement, and an accepted handoff to the team.

What You'll Bring

- Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or graduate degree in operations, engineering, business, supply chain, data and analytics, or a related field.

- Structured problem-solving skills and curiosity about how complex physical or technical systems work.

- Comfort with quantitative analysis, including spreadsheets and at least one data or automation tool such as SQL, Python, or a business-intelligence platform.

- Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to make complex information easy to understand.

- Evidence of following through on a project involving multiple contributors through coursework, work, research, or extracurricular experience.

- Comfort operating in ambiguity, asking good questions, incorporating feedback, and staying reliable on details.

- Ability to work onsite in South San Francisco and willingness to travel occasionally within the United States to support launches.

- Drive the first builds of flight hardware and work with a manufacturing team to establish a production line

- Coordinate and execute development, qualification, and acceptance testing of flight hardware

- Participate in design reviews internally and with suppliers and customers

- Partner with engineering and production teams to generate ideas, designs, and improvements for current and next-generation vehicles

• Support the development and integration of AI/ML models, LLM integrations, or intelligent services into controlled or production-like systems under guidance.
• Assist with data collection, preprocessing, transformation, and management to enable model training, testing, validation, and evaluation.

• Assist in ensuring AI systems and AI enabled features align with enterprise expectations for reliability, safety, governance, security, and compliance.
• Build foundational confidence working across AI-adjacent technology areas such as APIs, cloud environments, data platforms, CI/CD, containers, model deployment patterns, and monitoring.

AI Engineer Areas and Skills

AI Engineer Interns may support teams based on business needs, project requirements, and individual strengths. Experience in one or more of the following areas is beneficial:

• AI/Machine Learning Engineering: Python, R, Java, machine learning fundamentals, model training, model evaluation, feature engineering, NLP, embeddings, transformer models, LLM APIs, prompt engineering, retrieval
patterns, AI agents, model documentation, responsible AI concepts.
• Data Engineering for AI: Data collection, preprocessing, data quality, ETL, data pipelines, SQL, big data concepts, data validation, feature pipelines, and reproducible data workflows.
• AI-Enabled Software Engineering: APIs, microservices, inference endpoints, application integration, cloud-native development, agile delivery, testing, CI/CD, containerization, observability, and production-like deployment practices.
• Generative AI/LLM Applications: Prompt-based interactions, LLM integrations, retrieval-augmented generation concepts, evaluation of AI outputs, grounding patterns, guardrails, AI agents, agent orchestration, and human-in-the-loop review.
• Enterprise AI Readiness: Security, compliance, model governance, documentation, risk awareness, system reliability, issue escalation, and responsible AI practices.
• Cybersecurity & AI Security: Secure software development practices, application security fundamentals, identity and access management, data protection, encryption concepts, secure API design, vulnerability awareness, threat modeling fundamentals, secure use of AI/LLM technologies, AI security risks (prompt injection, data leakage, model abuse), governance controls, compliance awareness, and responsible handling of sensitive information.
